Songwriting & production

Jump to songwriting | Jump to production

I love making music. I want to transport listeners to a different world, to take you out of your daily head. I'm interested in collaborating more on both aspects, so have a read and listen below and get in touch if you want to.

Songwriting

Drama's what I want. Lots of song-based drama.

I'm not what you might call a 'normal' songwriter. I like playing different characters, on occasion I even play myself. I'm not interested in 'being cool' (good job, really).

Here's a load of songs of wildly varying sonic quality. Let me take you on a journey through space and time...

I've written daft, angry punk-influenced songs:

I've written rootsy, political songs...

And poetic creepy blues rock.

I sometimes write prettier, poppier songs:

I've co-written a concept album about a time-travelling Edward fop. First off, ABBA do post-punk with a bit of 1950s thrown in:

And then some dense disco (yes, that's me on the ludicrous falsetto):

I also like writing with strings (this is a theme tune for a film I made)...

...and this is a complicated orchestral arrangement I put together for a local artist:

Phew. And recently I've taken to writing more personally for one of my new albums. Dirty, dark and honest:

...to a song about J.D. f-ing Vance, some dance-infused political rock:

And the other of the albums has this gothic house track on it!

In summary

If you've got this far, bloody well done! I just want to create music that is varied and interesting, without worrying about genre, current taste or more or les anything. If you might want to collaborate then talk to me.

Production

Guise

This is a long distance collaboration with an old mate (Jim from uni).

For this one I had a descending bass riff & some idea of the vocal. I cut loops up to get the drums working & kept the arrangement sparse to highlight the how the melody, bass and Jim's piano accompaniment worked together.

And this one is a story song where I overdubbed loads of acoustics. I wanted that heavy electro-type beat with a big bass:

Holy Fools

This was for a now defunct band I was in where we had a load of unused tracking. I wanted to see what I could do with a couple of the recordings, for posterity more than anything. Here's our jazz metal one:

Out of the Rubble

This is my current project where I've done the most production work.

Aliens Stole our Women was a conceptual, collaborative E.P. involving a few folk: a drummer, two singers, my mate Chris on various synths & guitars (some of the songs are based around his stuff), a trumpet player and me on a variety of instruments.

This song was quite the production to put together: soooo many parts recorded at different times & in different spaces. It almost works, I properly bit off more than I could chew at the time:

This one's simpler (and arguably more successful):

I had a lot of fun putting this rather dark, surreal one together (based on a story I found on the internet) for my Early Mornings E.P. Most of it is actual drum programming (which I rarely do) but I liked the crunchy analogue feel of them, and the space of it:

I rarely do instrumentals so I set myself a challenge of using all found loops, samples and parts for the last song on my Channel Surfing E.P. I cheated in the end and wrote a chord sequence on the electric piano to hang everything off:

And let's end this part of the journey on a note of daft. This electro, Flaming Lips-inspired nonsense went through lots of different versions:
